title: Measuring the effects of danger signals on honey bee dopamine levels
author: Dong, Gu, et al.

steps.title: Secure source honey bee colonies
steps.instruction: Obtain multiple healthy Apis mellifera colonies from a beekeeper, each containing at least 20 Langstroth comb frames (23.18 cm high × 3.49 cm wide × 48.26 cm long) housed in two standard wood boxes (25.4 cm high × 53.34 cm wide × 41.59 cm deep) with approximately 45,000 bees and ample food, pollen, and brood.

steps.title: Select optimal foraging season and weather
steps.instruction: Choose a time of year when foragers are active (e.g., early fall or regional equivalent) and avoid cold, rain, or periods of excessive floral abundance that would hinder training at artificial feeders.

steps.title: Confirm predator availability
steps.instruction: Verify that the intended predator (e.g., hornets) is present during the planned experimental window; absence precludes the experiment.

steps.title: Gather required equipment and materials
steps.instruction: Collect all items listed in the protocol’s equipment section before beginning construction of observation hives and colonies.

steps.title: Build observation hives
steps.instruction: Construct each observation hive to the following specifications and install necessary components.

substeps.instruction: Cut a hive frame measuring 55.4 cm length × 17 cm width × 64 cm height.

Place two combs (43.5 cm × 23 cm each) taken from a fully established colony into the hive; one comb must contain brood with ~80 % coverage, the other must contain honey (~50 % coverage) and pollen (~50 % coverage), together with adult bees and the queen.
Install a tube through the hive wall with an inner diameter of 2–3 cm and a length of 25 cm to allow bee entry and exit.
Insert a wooden divider coated with beeswax to guide incoming bees toward one side of the lower comb, creating a “dance floor” for waggle‑dance observations.

steps.title: Assemble observation colonies
steps.instruction: Prepare three observation colonies using the built hives and combs.

substeps.instruction: Select two combs from a complete colony that include food, brood, adult bees, and the queen.
Carefully remove the glass cover and any protective doors from the observation hive.
Insert the selected combs into the hive, ensuring they are stable and correctly aligned.
Repeat steps a–c to establish a total of three observation colonies.

steps.title: Rest colonies before experiments
steps.instruction: Allow the newly established observation colonies to remain undisturbed for at least three days before any experimental manipulation.

steps.title: Analyze data with statistical software
steps.instruction: Process and interpret experimental data using JMP (SAS Institute) or R, applying the models described below.

substeps.instruction: For colony‑level data, fit a Univariate Repeated Measures Model with colony as the repeated measure and experimental phase as a fixed effect; log‑transform stop‑signal counts and feeder‑visit counts per 10 min if normality or homoscedasticity assumptions are violated.

For individual‑bee behaviors (stop signals, waggle‑dance circuits, hive‑visit duration), fit Repeated Measures Mixed Models using the REML algorithm, with colony as a random effect and bee identity nested within colony as another random effect; include experimental phase as a fixed effect and log‑transform response variables as needed.
To assess brain dopamine levels across bee types, fit a Mixed Model (REML) with colony as a random effect and bee type (control vs. experimental) as a fixed effect.
To evaluate dopamine supplementation, fit another Mixed Model (REML) with colony as a random effect and treatment type (control sucrose vs. sucrose + dopamine) as a fixed effect.
Inspect model residuals for each analysis and log‑transform additional variables (time on feeder, time inside hive, number of stop signals, number of waggle circuits) when required.

steps.title: Run REML mixed model for dopamine
steps.instruction: Specifically test the effect of dopamine supplementation on head dopamine concentration by fitting a Mixed Model with REML, using colony as a random effect and bee type (control sucrose‑fed vs. dopamine‑supplemented sucrose‑fed) as a fixed effect.
